issues.legal_issue: Compensation for acquired land must reflect whether it is similarly situated to land already valued and the distinct characteristics of other portions.
material_facts: The land was divided into six belts according to its quality and situation.
Land in the first four belts was found to be similarly circumstanced to other land acquired under the same notification for which compensation had been fixed at a higher rate.
The fifth-belt land was assessed separately, while the sixth-belt land was proved to consist of hillocks.
issues.conclusion: Compensation for the first four belts was fixed uniformly at the rate used for the comparable land; compensation for the fifth belt was increased to a reasonable rate; and the existing lower rate for the hillock land was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: The Court compared the circumstances and characteristics of the acquired land with comparable land and assessed compensation accordingly. It relied on the prior appellate determination concerning the comparable land, which had been affirmed by the Supreme Court, and found no basis to disturb the assessment for land proved to consist of hillocks.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_appeal and (first_four_belts_similarly_situated_to_comparable_land or fifth_belt_requires_separate_assessment or sixth_belt_proved_to_be_hillocks)

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The case is an appeal seeking increased compensation for acquired land.
predicates.first_four_belts_similarly_situated_to_c: The claimant's land in the first four belts is similarly situated to other land whose compensation was fixed at a higher rate.
predicates.fifth_belt_requires_separate_assessment: The land in the fifth belt has circumstances warranting a separate compensation assessment.
predicates.sixth_belt_proved_to_be_hillocks: The evidence establishes that the land in the sixth belt consists of hillocks.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns compensation for acquired land and the land portions are comparable to other valued land or have distinct established characteristics, the compensation is adjusted to reflect those circumstances.

issues.legal_issue: The enhanced solatium rate does not apply to an appeal where the underlying acquisition awards fall outside the statutory transitional interval.
material_facts: The Collector made the award in 1968 and the reference court made its award in 1972, both before the statutory transitional interval identified by the Court.
The claimants sought increased compensation in an appeal decided after those awards.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to solatium at the rate applicable when the awards were made, not the enhanced rate.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 23(2) and 30(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended by the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984, enhanced solatium applies where the Collector's or court's award was made during the statutory transitional interval, including appeals against such awards. Union of India v. Raghubir Singh was followed; K. Kamalajammanniavaru v. Special Land Acquisition Officer was approved, while Bhag Singh v. Union Territory of Chandigarh and State of Punjab v. Mohinder Singh were treated as overruled.

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: The case is an appeal concerning compensation for land acquired under compulsory acquisition proceedings.
predicates.collector_and_reference_awards_outside_t: The Collector's award and the reference court's award were both made outside the interval specified for transitional application of the enhanced solatium rate.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns compulsory acquisition and both underlying awards fall outside the transitional interval, solatium is limited to the rate applicable when the award was made.

issues.legal_issue: Interest on enhanced compensation remains at the original rate through the day before the amended interest provisions began to operate.
material_facts: Possession of the acquired land had been taken before the amendment to the interest provisions.
The Collector's and reference court's awards were made before the statutory transitional interval.
The judges agreed that interest on the enhanced compensation was payable at the original rate up to the day before the amendment came into force.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to interest at the original rate through September 23, 1984.
issues.legal_principle: Section 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as originally enacted, provided interest at six per cent per annum on excess compensation. The judges agreed on that rate through September 23, 1984. The judgment also considered section 30(2) of the 1984 Amendment Act and Union of India v. Raghubir Singh when addressing the temporal reach of the amendments.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The case is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_awarded: The appellate court increases the compensation payable for the acquired land.
predicates.interest_period_ends_before_amended_rate: The interest period at issue ends before the amended interest rate begins to apply.

issues.definition: When an appeal increases compensation and the interest period ends before the amended rate begins to apply, interest remains at the original rate for that period.

issues.legal_issue: The applicable interest rate on enhanced compensation after the amended provisions took effect, including any increased rate for delayed payment, requires resolution where the judges disagree.
material_facts: The underlying awards were made before the statutory transitional interval, and the appellate court increased the compensation.
One judge considered that the amended rate should apply from the amendment's commencement and proposed a further increased rate if payment was not made within a specified time.
The other judge considered that the original rate should continue until payment and rejected both proposed increases.
issues.conclusion: The judges agreed on the interest rate only through September 23, 1984; because they disagreed about the rate thereafter and about the proposed increase for delayed payment, the matter was referred to a larger bench.
issues.legal_principle: The majority opinion considered section 28 and the transitional provision in section 30(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, as amended, and reasoned that the continuing loss from delayed payment justified applying the amended rate prospectively. The dissent relied on the text of those provisions and Union of India v. Raghubir Singh, reasoning that the applicable rate was governed by the date of the underlying award. The judges did not resolve this disagreement.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The case is an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.enhanced_compensation_awarded: The appellate court increases the compensation payable for the acquired land.
predicates.underlying_awards_precede_transitional_i: The underlying awards were made before the statutory interval governing transitional application of the amended provisions.
predicates.judges_disagree_on_post_amendment_intere: The judges reach different conclusions about the interest rate after the amended provisions take effect or about a further increase for delayed payment.

issues.definition: When an appeal increases compensation, the underlying awards precede the transitional interval, and the judges disagree on post-amendment interest, that interest issue is referred to a larger bench.
